summary: Tested Phase 2 (AI document reading) and Phase 3 (printable summary), and re-ran the Phase 1 regression. Backend: 35 of 36 pytest tests pass. That covers the Phase 1 regression (20/20) and the new extraction suite (15 of 16). The extraction tests made real LLM calls, each taking about 3-5 seconds. Passing: 422 validation (empty text, missing label, bad kind/date); retry on an unknown source returns 404; partners get 403 on readings/project. Reading the quote gives Redwood capacity 1/2/4 with verbatim excerpts and line numbers, and no capacity reading comes from '2-man crew'. Reading the email makes the week 1 and 2 readings 0 from the email, with conflict=true and the quote facts superseded. Week 3 stays 4. The injected instruction is listed in ignored_instructions, and no $1 budget ceiling is proposed. An invalid correction ('abc') returns 422 and nothing changes. Correction history keeps the original value, prior/new values, who and when. Applying a superseded fact returns 422 'a later source changes this reading'. A stale rev returns 409. Applying an applied fact returns 422. After applying, gap week 1 goes from 7 to 6 and the candidate is recalculated as v2. With partner links, the candidate opens as an amendment preview instead. Reject works: the quote reading becomes current again. Retry re-reads. Frontend (1920 and 390px): demo login, the Read a document tab and the sample buttons work. Reads show the status 'Read'. Readings show 'Sources disagree', 'superseded by a later source', source label, line and excerpt. The ignored-instruction banner appears. Error paths work: .pdf and .docx are rejected and the typed text is kept; a .txt file loads into the textarea and fills the label; empty or label-missing submits show 422 errors and keep the input. Correcting with 'abc' shows an error; '2' then '0' shows 'Corrected by you', the original reading and both change lines with timestamps. Reject and apply work, the toast says 'Readings used. Candidate v2 recalculated.' and gap week 1 shows 6. /summary (via decide-summary-link) shows date, checks, contributions, exact responses and conditions. The print button calls window.print once. A partner opening /summary sees summary-error. No horizontal overflow at 390px on the Read tab or the summary page. Found 1 real logic bug (re-read overrides corrections) and 1 robustness bug (a malformed LLM fact crashes the read and leaves the source stuck).

critical.issue: Re-reading a source silently overrides the organizer's correction. run_extraction deletes only proposed/invalid facts, so corrected, applied and rejected facts stay. It then inserts new proposed facts with the same source_order and a later created_at. readings_from sorts by (source_order, created_at), so the new proposed value becomes the current reading. Reproduced: correcting email week 2 from 0 to 1, then retry, makes the current reading 'proposed 0' again. A rejected reading also comes back as a new proposed reading, and applied facts get duplicates from the same source. Test: TestPreviewAndReread.

Malformed but parseable LLM output crashes the request outside the try/except. The source stays in status 'reading' forever, and retry then returns 409 'already being read' permanently, with no failure message. Reproduced with make_fact in a unit check: partner='(Synthetic)' -> IndexError (n.split()[0] on an empty string in match_partner); note=5 -> TypeError (slicing an int); site=9 or excerpt=123 -> AttributeError .strip. A string week such as '1' is marked invalid instead of being coerced. This breaks the spec that failures keep the input, offer a retry and never claim success.

minor.issue: The LLM call runs inside the request (timeout 120s). If the worker restarts mid-read, status stays 'reading' for good, because nothing resets stale 'reading' sources. Consider a reading_started_at timestamp and letting retry proceed after the timeout.

Corrections are allowed on applied or rejected facts through the API. The UI hides the buttons, but the backend does not check status. A corrected applied fact goes back to 'corrected' and can be applied again.

ui_bugs.issue: Edit input state is useState(f.value), which is never re-synced. After a re-read or a correction elsewhere, the edit box shows a stale value. Low impact.
reader.onload uses the stale `f` closure. Edits typed into label or kind while the file loads are overwritten. Use the functional setF((prev) => ...). Low impact.

issues: The sticky dark 'Use selected readings' bar floats over the Documents list and readings while you scroll. On mobile it covers about 100px of content. Consider adding bottom padding to the panel equal to the bar height.
Document date uses the native input type=date, not the shadcn date picker (also flagged in iteration 1).
The Contributions table has 5 columns and gets very cramped at 390px. Site lists wrap to one token per line. Consider a stacked card layout on small screens (it fits; no overflow).
'Prepared Oct 24, 4:19 PM PT' has no year. A dated printable record should include the year.

action_items: HIGH: On re-read, keep organizer decisions. Either keep corrected/rejected facts as the reading for their target (prefer corrected over a new proposed fact from the same source), or skip creating new facts for targets already corrected or rejected from that source. Also avoid duplicates of applied facts.

HIGH: In run_extraction, wrap fact building (make_fact and the lists) in try/except and call fail() on any exception, so the source never stays in 'reading'. Harden make_fact: coerce non-string partner/site/excerpt/note with str(), guard match_partner against an empty name (n.split() empty), and accept string week digits.
MEDIUM: Let retry recover sources stuck in 'reading' longer than LLM_TIMEOUT.

LOW: Backend PUT /facts/{id} should reject corrections on applied or rejected facts, or define the behaviour. Re-sync FactLine edit state. Use a functional setF in pickFile. Add the year to the summary date. Make the summary contributions table mobile-friendly. Add padding under the sticky apply bar.
critical_code_review_comments: extract_routes.run_extraction: only the LLM call and parse are inside try/except. Fact creation, insert_many and the update run unprotected after status='reading' is set.
extract_routes.match_partner: pn.split()[0] == n.split()[0] raises IndexError when the model returns only '(Synthetic)' or whitespace as the partner.
extract_routes.readings_from: precedence uses only (source_order, created_at) and ignores status. Organizer corrections should outrank a re-proposed value from the same source.
The prompt-injection defence works: the system prompt treats the document as data, ignored instructions are surfaced, and the CREW_SIZE_RE guard catches crew-size capacity.
extract_routes.py (388 lines) and project_routes.py (451 lines) are within size limits. generate_candidate is reused cleanly by draft and apply.

success_rate.backend: 97% (35/36; the 1 failure is the real re-read/correction bug)
success_rate.frontend: 100% of the requested UI flows work

context_for_next_testing_agent: Run pytest /app/backend/tests/ (xdist loadscope is set in pytest.ini; use -n 0 for a single file). test_extract_summary.py makes real LLM reads (about 3-5s each, 5 reads). TestPreviewAndReread::...reread_keeps_correction should pass once the re-read precedence fix lands. To check the robustness fix, call extract_routes.make_fact with partner='(Synthetic)', note=5 or site=9. These must not raise, or run_extraction must call fail(). The UI flows were verified with readings-table row testids like reading-capacity-redwood-1 and reading-select-{factId}.
rca of the issue: Re-read override: retry_source -> run_extraction deletes facts with status in [proposed, invalid] only, then inserts fresh proposed facts for the same source. readings_from groups by target and picks usable[-1] after sorting by (source_order, created_at). The fresh fact has the same source_order and a later created_at, so it beats the organizer's corrected fact. Reproduce: read quote and email, correct email week 2 to 1, POST /sources/{email}/retry; the week 2 reading becomes proposed 0. Mitigation: sort so that corrected facts win within the same source, or delete/replace all non-applied facts and carry corrections forward by target. Stuck reading: make_fact exceptions happen after status='reading' is set and outside try/except, so the request returns 500 and retry then returns 409 forever.
